# Stellar Developer Docs

- [Build (193 pages)](https://developers.stellar.org/_llms/build.txt): Documentation for Build.

## Learn

###  

- [Glossary](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/glossary.md): Explore a comprehensive glossary of blockchain terms. Learn key concepts, definitions, and technical terms to better understand the Stellar network and ecosystem.

#### Core Concepts

- [Core Concepts](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/index.md): Learn the fundamentals and key concepts of the Stellar blockchain, including data structures, fees, consensus, anchors, Stellar Ecosystem Proposals, and more.
- [Stellar Stack](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-stack.md): Explore the core components and architecture of the Stellar stack, and see how they work together to power a fast, scalable, and decentralized network.
- [Lumens (XLM)](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/lumens.md): Learn about lumens (XLM), the native digital asset of the Stellar network. Understand its role in transactions, network fees, and smart contract rent.
- [Stellar Consensus Protocol](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-consensus-protocol.md): A brief overview of how the Stellar Consensus Protocol (SCP), a proof of agreement protocol, enables consensus and validates transactions on the network.
- [Liquidity on Stellar: Stellar Decentralized Exchange & Liquidity Pools](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/liquidity-on-stellar-sdex-liquidity-pools.md): Learn how liquidity pools enable trading on the Stellar Decentralized Exchange. Understand how they work, provide liquidity, and enable decentralized asset swaps on the network.
- [Fees, Resource Limits, and Metering](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/fees-resource-limits-metering.md): Learn how fees, resource limits, and metering work on the Stellar network. Understand cost structures, transaction pricing, and smart contract resource limits.
- [Stellar Ecosystem Proposals (SEPs)](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-ecosystem-proposals.md): Learn about Stellar Ecosystem Proposals (SEPs), standards that enhance interoperability, improve functionality, and expand the network's capabilities.
- [Anchors](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/anchors.md): Learn about the on and off ramps on Stellar called anchors and their role in bridging between the traditional financial system and blockchain networks.

##### Stellar Data Structures

- [Stellar Data Structures](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-data-structures/index.md): Learn about blockchain data structures, including accounts, transactions, assets, and ledgers. Understand how they work together to make the network function.
- [Ledgers](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-data-structures/ledgers.md): A ledger captures the state of the Stellar network at a point in time, storing accounts, balances, orders, smart contract data, and other persistent information.
- [Events](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-data-structures/events.md): Monitor off-chain movement of value and smart contract changes.
- [Accounts](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-data-structures/accounts.md): Learn about accounts on the Stellar network, including how they store balances, sign transactions, and interact with assets, smart contracts, and other features.
- [Assets on Stellar: Explore Trustlines, Smart Contract Integration & More](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-data-structures/assets.md): Learn how assets work on the Stellar network, including issuing, transferring, and managing tokens. Explore trustlines, using assets in smart contracts, & more.
- [Smart Contracts](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/stellar-data-structures/contracts.md): A smart contract is a programmed set of executable code and state that can be invoked on the Stellar network.

##### Operations & Transactions

- [Operations & Transactions](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/transactions/index.md): Learn about transactions on Stellar: how they work, the transaction lifecycle, a list of operations, and how they transfer assets and execute smart contracts.
- [Operations and Transactions](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/transactions/operations-and-transactions.md): Learn how operations and transactions work on the Stellar network. Understand how multiple operations are bundled into transactions to execute blockchain actions.
- [List of Operations](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/transactions/list-of-operations.md): Explore the full list of Stellar operations, including creating accounts, making payments, creating trustlines, all smart contract operations, and more.
- [Signatures and Multisig](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/transactions/signatures-multisig.md): This section details signing non-smart contract transactions.
- [Transaction Lifecycle](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/transactions/transaction-lifecycle.md): A user creates a transaction by setting the source account, sequence number, list of operations and their respective parameters, fee or fee-bump, and...

##### Smart Contracts

- [Smart Contracts](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/index.md): Overview of Contract Development.
- [Overview](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/overview.md): This section provides an overview of Stellar contracts, outlining their key concepts of smart contracts on the Stellar network.
- [Contract Rust Dialect](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/rust-dialect.md): Differences between Soroban Rust and typical Rust programming.
- [Environment Concepts](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/environment-concepts.md): The interface that defines objects, functions, and data available to smart contracts.
- [Authorization](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/authorization.md): Authorization is the process of judging which operations "should" or "should not" be allowed to occur; it is about judging _permission_.
- [Contract Lifecycle](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/contract-lifecycle.md): The process of developing, deploying, and maintaining smart contracts.

###### Contract Interactions

- [Contract Interactions](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/contract-interactions/index.md): Learn about the methods available for developers and users to interact with deployed contracts.
- [Overview](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/contract-interactions/overview.md): Interact with smart contracts.
- [Cross-Contract](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/contract-interactions/cross-contract.md): Interact with a Soroban contract from within another Soroban contract.
- [Tests](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/contract-interactions/tests.md): Interacting with contracts in tests
- [Stellar Transaction](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/contract-interactions/stellar-transaction.md): Invoke and deploy smart contracts with the InvokeHostFunctionOp operation.
- [Transaction Simulation](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/contract-interactions/transaction-simulation.md): Simulate a contract interaction contained in a Stellar transaction.

###### Types

- [Types](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/types/index.md): Learn about the types and data structures available to developers in Soroban smart contracts.
- [Built-In Types](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/types/built-in-types.md): Built-in types used as smart contract inputs and outputs.
- [Custom Types](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/types/custom-types.md): Struct, union, and enum types defined by contracts.
- [Fully-Typed Contracts](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/types/fully-typed-contracts.md): Smart contract WASM files contain a machine-readable description of the interface type.

###### Storage

- [Storage](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/storage/index.md): Overview of Storage.
- [Persisting Data](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/storage/persisting-data.md): Store and access smart contract data.
- [State Archival](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/storage/state-archival.md): Smart contract state archival.

###### Errors and Debugging

- [Errors and Debugging](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/errors-and-debugging/index.md): In-depth explanations and articles concerning specific topics of interest.
- [Generate Contract Errors](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/errors-and-debugging/errors.md): Generating errors from smart contracts.
- [Debugging Modes](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/errors-and-debugging/debugging.md): Debug smart contracts natively and as WASM.
- [Debugging Contract Errors](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/contract-development/errors-and-debugging/debugging-errors.md): Debug and Understanding Soroban Errors through the General Transaction Cycle.

##### Data Format

- [Data Format](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/data-format/index.md): Learn how Stellar represents and exchanges data.
- [XDR](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/data-format/xdr.md): Understand Stellar's XDR binary format, why it exists, and how to inspect or parse it safely.
- [XDR-JSON](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/fundamentals/data-format/xdr-json.md): Use the XDR-JSON schema to round-trip Stellar XDR payloads through JSON tools without losing fidelity.

#### Migrate from Another Chain

- [Migrate from Another Chain](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/migrate/index.md): Adapt your existing projects to work with Stellar.

##### EVM Networks

- [EVM Networks](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/migrate/evm/index.md): Adapt your existing Ethereum-compatible smart contracts to work with Stellar.
- [Introduction](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/migrate/evm/introduction-to-solidity-and-rust.md): Explore the fundamentals of Solidity, Rust, and Soroban.
- [Getting Started with Rust and Solidity](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/migrate/evm/solidity-and-rust-basics.md): Explore the fundamentals of Solidity and Rust Syntax, Data Types, and Basic Constructs.
- [Advanced Smart Contract Concepts with Solidity and Rust](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/migrate/evm/solidity-and-rust-advanced-concepts.md): Learn advanced Solidity and Rust concepts and write safe and efficient smart contracts.
- [Smart Contract Development with Soroban and Hardhat](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/migrate/evm/smart-contract-deployment.md): Explore advanced Solidity and Soroban concepts, craft secure and efficient Soroban smart contracts and deploy and test your contracts in a testnet environment.
- [Solidity support via Solang](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/migrate/evm/solidity-support-via-solang.md): Compile Solidity contracts to Wasm for Stellar using the Solang compiler.

#### Interactive Learning

- [Interactive Learning](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/interactive/index.md): Learn by doing in this collection of resources designed to get you up and running on the Stellar network in no time!
- [Stellar Quest](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/interactive/quest.md): Stellar Quest teaches you about Stellar operations and fundamentals in a gamified experience.
- [Fast, Cheap, and 0ut 0f Control](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/interactive/fca00c.md): Fast, Cheap, and 0ut 0f Control (FCA00C) is a collection of games and tutorials designed to familiarize you with smart contracts on the Stellar network.
- [Master Rust Smart Contract Development on Stellar](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/learn/interactive/dapp-world.md): Learn to develop secure, efficient smart contracts on the Stellar network using Rust.

## Tokens

###  

- [Issuing Assets vs. Creating Custom Tokens: Key Differences & Best Practices](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/index.md): Learn about the differences between issuing assets on the Stellar network, creating smart contract tokens, and information and best practices for each.
- [Assets Overview & Comparison](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/anatomy-of-an-asset.md): Asset Overview and Comparison of Stellar Asset (with SAC), SEP-41 Contract Token, and T-REX (Token for Regulated Exchanges)
- [Quickstart](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/quickstart.md): Issue your first asset on the Stellar network in one, single transaction!
- [Asset Design Considerations](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/control-asset-access.md): It is best practice on the Stellar network to create two accounts when issuing an asset: 1) the issuing account and 2) the distribution account.
- [Use Issued Assets in Smart Contracts with the Stellar Asset Contract (SAC)](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/stellar-asset-contract.md): Learn to make payments and interact with assets issued on the Stellar network in smart contracts using the Stellar Asset Contract (SAC), a built-in contract.
- [Create Contract Tokens on Stellar: Standards & Integration](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/token-interface.md): Learn about and create contract tokens on the Stellar network. Learn about the standards, functionality, and integration of contract tokens.
- [Issue an Asset Tutorial](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/how-to-issue-an-asset.md): Learn how to issue a Stellar asset, set trustlines, and manage supply. Follow this step-by-step guide to create and distribute assets on the network.
- [Publish Information About An Asset](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/publishing-asset-info.md): Stellar assets are defined by who issued them, what they represent, and the terms and conditions for their use.
- [Cross-Chain USDC Transfers with CCTP](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/cross-chain-transfers.md): Use Circle's Cross-Chain Transfer Protocol (CCTP) to move native USDC between Stellar and other supported chains.
- [USDT0 Transfers with LayerZero](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tokens/usdt0-layerzero.md): Use USDT0, Tether's USDT delivered over LayerZero's OFT standard, on Stellar. Mainnet addresses, how LayerZero fits, integration pointers, and amount precision.

- [Data (305 pages)](https://developers.stellar.org/_llms/data.txt): Documentation for Data.

## Tools

###  

- [Tools Overview](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/index.md): Explore tools for building, testing, and deploying blockchain applications. Access SDKs, APIs, and utilities to streamline development on the Stellar network.
- [OpenZeppelin Relayer](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/openzeppelin-relayer.md): OpenZeppelin Relayer is an open source framework for submitting transactions to the Stellar network, and Stellar Channels is the managed service OpenZeppelin runs on top of it.
- [OpenZeppelin Contracts and Toolings](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/openzeppelin-contracts.md): OpenZeppelin Contract Library and Toolings
- [Scaffold Stellar](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/scaffold-stellar.md): Convention-over-configuration toolkit for Stellar smart contract development

#### SDKs

- [SDKs](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/sdks/index.md): Explore SDKs for building blockchain applications. Use JavaScript, Python, and more to interact with the Stellar network and streamline development.
- [Contract SDKs](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/sdks/contract-sdks.md): Contract SDKs are used to build smart contracts that will be deployed to the Stellar network.
- [Client & XDR SDKs](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/sdks/client-sdks.md): Explore the Stellar SDK library to simplify blockchain development. Leverage Rust, JavaScript, Python, and more to build on and integrate with the network.
- [Build Your Own Contract SDK](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/sdks/build-your-own.md): This is for building an SDK for writing smart contracts.

#### Stellar CLI

- [Stellar CLI](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/index.md): The CLI for interacting with the Stellar network
- [Install the Stellar CLI](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/install-cli.md): How to Install the Stellar CLI.
- [Stellar CLI Manual](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/stellar-cli.md): This document contains the help content for the Stellar command-line program.
- [Plugins](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/plugins.md): How to Use Plugins with the Stellar CLI
- [Plugins List](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/plugins-list.md): See a list of published Stellar CLI plugin

##### Stellar CLI for Agents

- [Stellar CLI for Agents](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/index.md): Use the Stellar CLI and CLI Skills to give your AI agents an agent-friendly wallet and native way to inspect, move, and manage assets on Stellar.
- [Quickstart](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/quickstart.md): Install the stellar CLI, connect it to your agent, fund a testnet key, and make your first agent-driven transfer.
- [Skills](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/skills.md): What the stellar skill subcommand gives your agent, what it leaves out, and an optional skill for broader Stellar development.

###### Agent Cookbook

- [Send tokens](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/send-tokens.md): Send the native asset or a classic asset with `stellar token transfer`, and confirm what shipped.
- [Check balances and metadata](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/check-balances-and-metadata.md): Read balances and token metadata with `stellar token balance`, `name`, `symbol`, and `decimals`, no key required.
- [Delegate spending](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/delegate-spending.md): How much can your agent spend without you, and what is the worst case if it goes wrong. A funded account, an allowance, a co-signed vault, a zero-XLM agent, and a self-expiring grant, compared honestly.
- [Sign messages](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/sign-messages.md): Sign and verify a message offline with `stellar message sign` and `stellar message verify`, SEP-53.
- [Build and submit transactions](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/build-and-submit-transactions.md): Build unsigned transactions with `--build-only`, sign and inspect them offline, then submit with `stellar tx`.
- [Pay for APIs with x402](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/pay-for-apis-x402.md): Pay for x402-protected APIs on Stellar with USDC, using the stellar CLI only for the identity and the SEP-41 settlement rail.
- [USDT0 on mainnet](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/usdt0-on-mainnet.md): Work with USDT0 on Stellar mainnet from the CLI. Addresses, trustlines, the clawback flags, and how to acquire it safely.
- [Build and deploy a contract](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/guides/build-and-deploy-contracts.md): Have your agent create a contract project with `stellar contract init`, build, deploy, and invoke it, and use the `AGENTS.md` file the project ships with.

###### Reference

- [Architecture](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/reference/architecture.md): How the Stellar CLI is put together, where it keeps state, how read and write paths differ, and how an agent connects to it.
- [Authority & Security Model](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/reference/authority-model.md): What bounds an agent's spending authority when it drives the Stellar CLI, which controls exist today, and which do not.
- [Output and errors](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/reference/output-and-errors.md): Which stellar commands support --output and which values each accepts, the token family's typed error envelope, and how every other command reports failure.
- [Troubleshooting](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/agent-cli/reference/troubleshooting.md): Start with stellar doctor, then fix funding, trustline, network, and signing errors your agent will hit with the stellar CLI.

##### Cookbook

- [Cookbook](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/index.md): Guides that will help you use the Stellar CLI.
- [Asset Management](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/asset-management.md): Issue a Stellar Asset, deploy it's contract, and mint, burn, freeze, and clawback.
- [Add meta data to contract WASM on build](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/contract-build-meta.md): Include meta data in the contract WASM byte code on build
- [Contract Invoke: Argument Types](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/contract-invoke-arguments.md): How to pass each argument type when invoking a Stellar smart contract using the CLI
- [Contract Lifecycle](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/contract-lifecycle.md): Manage the lifecycle of a Stellar smart contract using the CLI
- [Deploy a contract from uploaded Wasm bytecode](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/deploy-contract.md): Deploy an instance of a compiled contract that has already been uploaded on the network
- [Deploy the Stellar Asset Contract for a Stellar asset](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/deploy-stellar-asset-contract.md): Deploy an SAC for a Stellar asset so that it can interact with smart contracts
- [Extend a deployed contract instance's TTL](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/extend-contract-instance.md): Use the CLI to extend the time to live (TTL) of a contract instance
- [Extend a deployed contract's storage entry TTL](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/extend-contract-storage.md): Use the CLI to extend the time to live (TTL) of a contract's persistent storage entry
- [Extend a deployed contract's Wasm code TTL](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/extend-contract-wasm.md): Use Stellar CLI to extend contract's Wasm bytecode TTL, with or without local binary
- [Payments and Assets](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/payments-and-assets.md): Send XLM, stellar classic, or a soroban asset using the Stellar CLI
- [Restore an archived contract using the Stellar CLI](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/restore-contract-instance.md): Restore an archived contract instance using the Stellar CLI
- [Restore archived contract data using the Stellar CLI](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/restore-contract-storage.md): Restore archived contract storage entries using Stellar CLI
- [Stellar Keys](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/stellar-keys.md): Manage stellar keys
- [Create Claimable Balance](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/tx-new-create-claimable-balance.md): Create claimable balances with various claim predicates using the Stellar CLI
- [tx Commands](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/tx-new.md): Create stellar transactions using the Stellar CLI
- [tx op add](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/tx-op-add.md): Create stellar transactions using the Stellar CLI
- [tx sign and tx send](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/tx-sign.md): Create stellar transactions using the Stellar CLI
- [Upload and deploy a smart contract](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/upload-deploy.md): Combine the upload and deploy commands in the Stellar CLI to accomplish both tasks
- [Upload Wasm bytecode](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/cli/cookbook/upload-wasm.md): Use the Stellar CLI to upload a compiled smart contract on the ledger

#### Lab

- [Lab](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/index.md): Explore Lab, a developer tool to learn about the Stellar network
- [Account](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/account.md): Explore Stellar Lab's Account Page by creating and funding account on Stellar
- [Transactions](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/transactions.md): Explore Stellar Lab's Build Transaction Page by creating and submitting a transaction on Stellar
- [Transaction Dashboard](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/transaction-dashboard.md): Use Stellar Lab's Transaction Dashboard Page to get a comprehensive view of transaction details for both classic and smart contracts
- [Using Lab with Quickstart](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/quickstart-with-lab.md): Quickstart provides an easy way to set up a local Stellar network environment.

##### View XDR

- [View XDR](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/view-xdr/index.md): This section provides tools to work with XDR (External Data Representation) data. You can decode XDR into easy-to-read JSON format, convert JSON back into XDR format, or compare two XDR data sets to view their differences side-by-side.
- [XDR to JSON](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/view-xdr/xdr-to-json.md): The XDR to JSON converter transforms base-64 encoded XDR data into readable JSON format.
- [JSON to XDR](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/view-xdr/json-to-xdr.md): The JSON to XDR converter transforms JSON objects into base-64 encoded XDR format.
- [Diff XDRs](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/view-xdr/diff-xdr.md): The Diff XDRs tool compares two base-64 encoded XDRs and highlights the differences between them in JSON format.

##### Saved

- [Saved](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/saved/index.md): View keypairs, requests, and transactions saved in local storage.
- [Keypairs](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/saved/keypairs.md): View saved keypairs (accounts).
- [Requests](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/saved/requests.md): View saved Horizon endpoints and RPC methods.
- [Transactions](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/saved/transactions.md): View saved transactions.

##### API Explorer

- [Developer Tools](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/api-explorer/index.md): This section demonstrates how to use RPC methods and Horizon endpoints on the Stellar Lab across different networks, including features like sharing URLs and saving requests for future use.
- [Horizon Endpoints](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/api-explorer/horizon-endpoint.md): Horizon is nearing end-of-life and will eventually be deprecated in favor of Stellar RPC and Portfolio APIs. While it will continue to receive updates to maintain compatibility with upcoming protocol releases, it won't receive new feature development. Consider switching to Stellar RPC or another dat…
- [RPC Methods](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/api-explorer/rpc-methods.md): RPC methods are a set of functions that allow developers to interact directly with the Stellar network.

##### Smart Contracts

- [Smart Contracts](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/smart-contracts/index.md): Stellar Lab provides a comprehensive suite of tools for exploring, testing, and interacting with smart contracts on the Stellar network. These tools are designed to help developers understand contract behavior, debug issues, and test contract interactions without writing additional code.
- [Contract Explorer](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/smart-contracts/contract-explorer.md): Explore and interact with deployed Stellar smart contracts through a browser-based interface. View contract specs, source code, storage, build info, version history, and invoke contract methods directly.
- [Smart Contract List](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/smart-contracts/smart-contract-list.md): A list of Stellar smart contracts on the selected network
- [Upload and Deploy Contract](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/lab/smart-contracts/upload-deploy-contract.md): Upload your contract's WASM bytecode and deploy the contract to the network.

#### Quickstart

- [Quickstart](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/index.md): Quickstart is a local Stellar network environment (node) for development and testing.
- [Explorer](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/explorer.md): Using Explorer When Lab runs in Quickstart
- [Network Modes](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/network-modes.md): Quickstart supports the network modes local, testnet, futurenet and pubnet
- [Faucet](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/faucet.md): Use the Friendbot faucet to fund accounts on Quickstart

##### Getting Started

- [Getting Started](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/getting-started/index.md): Use Stellar CLI to install Quickstart
- [Connect Stellar Lab](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/getting-started/connect-stellar-lab.md): Connect Quickstart to Stellar Lab
- [Deploy Smart Contract](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/getting-started/deploy-smart-contract.md): Deploy a smart contract to the Quickstart local network.

##### Debugging

- [Debugging](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/debugging/index.md): Use Quickstart for debugging
- [Diagnostic Events](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/debugging/diagnostic-events.md): Soroban diagnostic events contain logs about internal events
- [Viewing Logs](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/debugging/viewing-logs.md): View logs inside Quickstart the container

##### Cloud Deployment

- [Cloud Deployment](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/cloud/index.md): Quickstart can be deployed to any cloud to create a shareable test network
- [DigitalOcean](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/cloud/digitalocean.md): Deploy Quickstart to DigitalOcean
- [Fly.io](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/cloud/fly.io.md): Deploy Quickstart to fly.io

##### Advanced Usage

- [Advanced Usage](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/advanced-usage/index.md): Quickstart can be configured to your personal preferences and use cases
- [Container](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/advanced-usage/container.md): Quickstart is packaged as a docker container
- [Service Options](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/advanced-usage/service-options.md): Quickstart can be started with all services enabled, or with selected services enabled
- [Operation Modes](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/advanced-usage/operation-modes.md): Quickstart can operate in different modes for different use cases
- [Ports](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/advanced-usage/ports.md): Quickstart can operate in different modes for different use cases
- [Run Commands](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/quickstart/advanced-usage/run-command-examples.md): Examples of run commands for starting Quickstart in the different modes

- [Node Operator Tools](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/developer-tools/node-operator-tools.md): Explore a suite of developer tools for Stellar, including node operator tools.
- [Security Tools](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/developer-tools/security-tools.md): Explore a suite of security tools for Stellar developers.
- [Wallet Integration](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/developer-tools/wallets.md): Explore a suite of developer tools for Stellar wallets.

- [MoneyGram Ramps](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/tools/ramps/moneygram.md): MoneyGram Ramps is a MoneyGram product that enables users of third-party applications, such as crypto wallets and exchanges, to cash-in (deposit) and...

#### Infrastructure Tools

## Validators

###  

- [Validators Introduction](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/index.md): Learn how validators support network security and consensus. Understand their role, setup requirements, and how they help maintain the integrity of the Stellar network.
- [Tier 1 Organizations](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/tier-1-orgs.md): Tier 1 organizations are a group of organizations that bear the safety and liveness of the Stellar network on their shoulders. They earn this role because most other organizations on the network require agreement from them — by including them in their quorum sets — in order to commit to a new ledger…

#### Admin Guide

- [Admin Guide](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/index.md): Stellar Core is the program nodes use to communicate with other nodes to create and maintain the Stellar peer-to-peer network. It's an implementation of the Stellar Consensus Protocol configured to construct a chain of ledgers guaranteed to be in agreement across all participating nodes at all times…
- [Prerequisites](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/prerequisites.md): You can install Stellar Core a number of different ways, and once you do, you can configure it to participate in the network on a several different levels: it can be either a Basic Validator or a Full Validator. No matter how you install Stellar Core or what kind of node you run, however, you need t…
- [Installing](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/installation.md): There are three common ways to install and run Stellar Core.
- [Configuring](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/configuring.md): Before attempting to configure stellar-core, it is highly recommended to first try running a private network or joining the test network.
- [Environment Preparation](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/environment-preparation.md): Initialize the Database and Local State
- [Publishing History Archives](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/publishing-history-archives.md): If you want to run a Full Validator, you need to set up your node to publish a history archive covering the network's complete history. You can host an archive using a blob store such as Amazon's S3 or Digital Ocean's spaces, or you can simply serve a local archive directly via an HTTP server such a…
- [Running](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/running-node.md): Starting Your Node
- [Logging](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/logging.md): Stellar Core sends logs to standard error and stellar-core.log by default, configurable with the LOG_FILE_PATH field.
- [Monitoring](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/monitoring.md): Once your node is up and running, it's important to keep an eye on it to make sure it stays afloat and continues to contribute to the health of the overall...
- [Maintenance](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/maintenance.md): Maintenance here refers to anything involving taking your validator temporarily out of the network (to apply security patches, system upgrade, etc).
- [Upgrading the Network](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/network-upgrades.md): The network itself has network wide settings that can be updated.
- [Soroban Settings](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/soroban-settings.md): Soroban has a large collection of settings stored on-ledger that can be modified through a validator vote.
- [Commands](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/commands.md): Stellar Core can be controlled using a robust CLI.
- [Advanced](https://developers.stellar.org/docs/validators/admin-guide/advanced.md): This page contains information that is useful to know but that should not stop somebody from running a node.

- [Platforms (189 pages)](https://developers.stellar.org/_llms/platforms.txt): Documentation for Platforms.
